guard: Ctrl-C on a foreground `cotal up` follows the same sparing rule as bare `cotal down` (#1307): the seat snapshot is taken while the manager still answers, the exact recorded manager's spare capability is asserted before any signal, the teardown is awaited before the broker is signalled, and the seats left behind are reported with the reap route. The handler is idempotent under a second Ctrl-C.
why: The suite drives the shipped foreground `up` as a real subprocess with a real managed seat (a shim
`claude` on PATH resolving to a real core-dist mesh endpoint), so a mutant that arms the destructive
intent is observed as a DEAD SEAT PROCESS and one that ignores the refusal gate is observed as a
DEAD MANAGER AND BROKER, not inferred from a source string.
M1 (arm the intent) is the destructive regression this guard exists for. A bare arm is refused by
the shipped reservation gate, so the mutant writes the stop reservation itself before arming (and
carries its own dynamic import); the manager consumes a valid intent and reaps every managed seat.
The seat-survives cell is the named assertion.
M2 (remove the spared report) restores the pre-fix silence: the stack still tears down and the seat
still survives, but the operator is told nothing. Only the spared-report cell can notice.
M3 (drop the refusal gate's return) is the round-2 blocker: the refusal prints and the teardown
proceeds anyway. The refusal-gate cell names the red.
All mutations run the CLI as a subprocess, so they mutate a module only `dist/` delivers to it:
every mutation builds first and rebuilds in `afterRestore` (dist/ is gitignored; git cannot be the
recovery for a build compiled from the mutant).

mutations.name: M1 the handler arms the destructive shutdown intent with its own reservation, so the manager reaps every managed seat on Ctrl-C
mutations.expectRed: the seat SURVIVES the Ctrl-C teardown
mutations.cell: the seat SURVIVES the Ctrl-C teardown
mutations.note: The destructive shape #1307 guards against: the foreground handler publishing the one-shot with-agents intent before signalling the manager. A bare arm is refused by the shipped gate (it requires the stop reservation only cotal down's stopLocalProcess holds) and grades WRONG-RED on the refusal, so the mutant creates the reservation itself first, exactly as the destructive regression would have to; it carries its own dynamic import so the healthy tree needs no unused carrier. The manager's signal handler then consumes a valid v1 intent and mgr.stop({ withAgents: true }) reaps the seat, so the first cell that can notice is the seat-survives cell. Deterministic: the reservation write, the arm and the consume all succeed on every run.

mutations.name: M2 the handler stops reporting the seats it left behind
mutations.expectRed: the spared report names the seat and the reap route
mutations.cell: the spared report names the seat and the reap route
mutations.note: The pre-fix silence: teardown still works and the seat still survives, but the operator is told nothing about live work while bare `down` reports it. Only the spared-report cell can notice, so it is the named assertion; the snapshot is still taken, so no earlier cell moves.

mutations.name: M3 the refusal stops being the signal gate: the teardown proceeds after the bare-stop refusal
mutations.expectRed: the refusal gate leaves the manager and broker running
mutations.cell: the refusal gate leaves the manager and broker running
mutations.note: The round-2 blocker as a mutant: the refusal prints but the async teardown continues past the return, so the manager and the broker are signalled anyway and up exits 0. The refusal-gate cell (capability file removed, SIGINT, manager and broker still alive, refusal names the reap route, no spared report) is the first cell that can notice. Deterministic: the capability file is deleted by the cell before the signal.
